translationRepairs: The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Gao. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.

The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Wu. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.

s0152’s 言之世祖 / 世祖嘉其義 names Shizu, the temple title of Southern Qi Emperor Wu (Xiao Ze), not Emperor Gao (太祖). Replacing Emperor Gao with Emperor Wu corrects the misidentification and leaves the rest of the idiomatic intact.

The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to the Founding Emperor; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. The Founding Emperor admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.

The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to Emperor Wu; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. Emperor Wu admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.
The same unit twice refers to 世祖, Emperor Wu, not the founding emperor (太祖). The proposed literal correctly substitutes Emperor Wu for Founding Emperor in both places.
Emperor Gao said: "These are all acts of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."
Emperor Wu said: "These are all acts of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."
s0154’s 世祖曰 continues the same Shizu of the preceding units—Emperor Wu, not Emperor Gao. The proposed speaker label is accurate and otherwise unchanged.
The Founding Emperor said: "These are all matters of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."
Emperor Wu said: "These are all matters of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."
世祖曰 is Emperor Wu speaking; Founding Emperor misreads the temple title as 太祖. Emperor Wu is the correct literal rendering here.

In the fifth year of Yongming Emperor Gao decreed: "Xiao Ruiming, Flying Dragon General, central army aide of the Anxi army, and magistrate of Songzi, loved his parents with pure devotion, served them with joyful ritual care, and mourned so deeply that he destroyed himself.

In the fifth year of Yongming Emperor Wu decreed: "Xiao Ruiming, Flying Dragon General, central army aide of the Anxi army, and magistrate of Songzi, loved his parents with pure devotion, served them with joyful ritual care, and mourned so deeply that he destroyed himself.
永明五年，世祖詔曰 places the edict under Yongming, Emperor Wu’s reign era; 世祖 is therefore Emperor Wu, not Emperor Gao. The name correction matches the Chinese.

In the fifth year of Yongming, the Founding Emperor issued an edict: "The Flying Dragon General, Central Army Aide of the Anxi Army, and Magistrate of Songzi, Xiao Ruiming, loved and revered with pure depth, nourished his parents with cheerful countenance and full ritual, and in mourning exceeded proper grief until he destroyed himself.

In the fifth year of Yongming, Emperor Wu issued an edict: "The Flying Dragon General, Central Army Aide of the Anxi Army, and Magistrate of Songzi, Xiao Ruiming, loved and revered with pure depth, nourished his parents with cheerful countenance and full ritual, and in mourning exceeded proper grief until he destroyed himself.
永明五年，世祖詔曰 identifies Shizu issuing a Yongming-era edict—Emperor Wu, not the founding emperor. The proposed literal correctly replaces Founding Emperor with Emperor Wu.
Emperor Gao appointed him reader to Prince Zilin of Nankang.
Emperor Wu appointed him reader to Prince Zilin of Nankang.
s0209’s 世祖以為南康王子琳侍讀 attributes the appointment to Shizu (Emperor Wu), not Emperor Gao. The proposed idiomatic corrects only that misnaming.
The Founding Emperor appointed him Reader to the Prince of Nankang, Zilin.
Emperor Wu appointed him Reader to the Prince of Nankang, Zilin.
世祖 in this appointment is Emperor Wu; Founding Emperor wrongly equates him with 太祖. The proposed literal restores the correct ruler.
He Yin and Xie Tiao were then in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they wrote urging him not to destroy himself in grief.
He Yin and Xie Fei were then in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they wrote urging him not to destroy himself in grief.
s0236 names 謝朏, Xie Fei; Xie Tiao is a different person written 謝朓. The proposed idiomatic corrects the personal name without other changes.
At the time He Yin and Xie Tiao were both in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him against destroying himself.
At the time He Yin and Xie Fei were both in seclusion on Eastern Mountain; they sent letters earnestly admonishing him against destroying himself.
The focus unit’s 謝朏 is Xie Fei, not Xie Tiao (謝朓). The proposed literal restores the correct name while preserving the rest of the sentence.
Yet honoring gates, renaming lanes, sending grain, and maintaining granaries amounted to little more than pity for widows and orphans and rewards for diligent farmers.
Yet honoring gates, renaming lanes, sending grain, and maintaining granaries amounted to little more than pity for widowers and widows and rewards for diligent farmers.
不過鰥寡齊矜 uses 鰥寡, the standard pair for widowers and widows; “widows and orphans” invents orphans absent from this phrase. The proposed idiomatic matches the Chinese and the already-correct literal.
